title: The Summit of the Coral Triangle
premise: Coral Crane, a bush pilot ferrying medicine and secrets across the Coral Triangle, has spent a decade outrunning the memory of the dive accident that killed her partner and her own testimony that sent his brother to prison. When an earthquake tide exposes a cave holding a Spanish galleon's manifest — and proof her testimony was wrong — she is dragged into a race against a ruthless salvage fleet, a marine archaeologist who knew her partner, and the monsoon bearing down on all of them. Over six tides, Coral must choose between protecting the lie that keeps her flying and the truth that could free a man and damn herself. She beats the fleet by hours, surrenders the wreck's evidence to authorities at the cost of her license, and finally stops moving — choosing love and accountability over escape.
about_author: Tamsin Halloran is a former charter pilot turned novelist who spent five years living aboard a ketch in Southeast Asian waters. Her fiction draws on real tides, real storms, and the people who live one weather system from ruin.

chapters.title: Fuel, Rumors, and Rain
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She flies quinine and gossip into a river village, establishing her rule: never land twice in the same place. A passenger mentions strange lights on Karakel Island before the quake season. Emotional beat: restless competence masking dread; Coral refuses an invitation to stay the night.

chapters.title: The Tide That Opens Doors
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. An earthquake drops the sea off Karakel, revealing a sea cave mouth never charted. Forced down by engine trouble, she shelters there overnight and finds carved coral, a rotted chest, and a lead manifest sheet stamped with her late partner's expedition mark. Beat: awe curdling into recognition.

chapters.title: What the Manifest Says
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, flashback woven in. The manifest lists artifacts recovered years ago — including the compass she testified was lost in the dive that killed Mateo. If it exists here, her sworn account was false. Beat: guilt resurfacing like a body she buried too shallow.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Weather buoys confirm a monsoon landfall in six tidal cycles; after that, the cave floods permanently. She calculates fuel, distance, and lies to herself about why she's going back. Beat: decision made under the alibi of duty.

chapters.title: The Salvage Fleet
chapters.summary: Vikram Rao's POV, captain of the salvage vessel Sable Fortune. He has a leaked copy of the same manifest and orders to strip the site before any government survey. His crew includes a diver who recognizes Coral's plane. Beat: cold professional menace with a flicker of conscience.

chapters.title: Dr. Ilsa Reyes
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. A marine archaeologist arrives at Coral's airstrip asking about Karakel — and reveals she was Mateo's research partner, and that Mateo wrote to her weeks before he died claiming the expedition logs were forged. Beat: grief meeting suspicion; two women circling the same wound.

chapters.title: Unwelcome Passenger
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Against every instinct, Coral flies Ilsa toward Karakel because Ilsa can read the manifest's cipher. Mid-flight they spot the Sable Fortune heading the same way. Beat: reluctant alliance sealed by shared enemy and shared dead man.

chapters.title: Tide One: The Descent
chapters.summary: Coral and Ilsa's alternating POV. They enter the cave at slack water, mapping chambers and finding Mateo's personal slate — his handwriting, dated after the 'final' dive. Beat: hope as a dangerous current pulling them deeper.

chapters.title: Tide Two: The Fleet Arrives
chapters.summary: Vikram's POV. The Sable Fortune anchors off Karakel; Vikram sends divers into the cave and finds signs someone got there first. He chooses not to report it — yet. Beat: the hunter hesitating, intrigued rather than enraged.

chapters.title: The Brother
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Radio contact with Rafe, Mateo's brother, four years into his sentence, who begs her not to dig — some truths, he says, cost more than the lie did. Beat: loyalty versus truth made flesh in one phone call.

chapters.title: Tide Three: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Someone slashes the plane's tires and steals their spare air tanks. Coral suspects Vikram; Ilsa suspects the third member of Mateo's old expedition, Dez Okafor, who vanished after the accident. Beat: paranoia tightening like a wet rope.

chapters.title: Dez Okafor Lives
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. Hiding on Karakel since the 'accident,' Dez confesses via note left in the cave: he forged the logs under pressure from the expedition's financier, and Mateo found out. Beat: cowardice seeking absolution at the worst possible moment.

chapters.title: Tide Four: The Standoff
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Vikram corners them at the cave mouth with the manifest sheet in hand. Instead of violence, he offers a deal: split the salvage value, bury the forgery story. Beat: temptation priced in freedom and fuel money.

chapters.title: What Coral Buried
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, long flashback. The full night of the dive: her panic, her false statement, why she let Rafe take the blame for negligence that wasn't his. Beat: the confession she's been flying away from for a decade, finally spoken aloud to Ilsa.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa realizes turning in the evidence frees Rafe but ends Coral's flying career and exposes Ilsa's own suppressed findings. She and Coral admit what's growing between them even as the barometer falls. Beat: tenderness chosen with the storm already audible.

chapters.title: Tide Five: The Fleet Strikes
chapters.summary: Vikram's POV then Coral's. Vikram's crew blasts the cave entrance wider to speed extraction, collapsing a chamber where Dez is trapped. Coral dives into the flooding dark to reach him. Beat: courage as reflex — the woman who runs runs toward.

chapters.title: Monsoon Landfall
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The storm hits early; the Sable Fortune drags anchor, Vikram's crew mutinies, and Coral's plane is the only way out for injured divers. Beat: enemies thrown together by weather, debts suddenly payable only in rescue.

chapters.title: Tide Six: The Last Window
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Between storm cells, Coral flies three loads of survivors out, then returns for the manifest and Mateo's slate as the final tide seals the cave forever. Beat: everything risked on one runway of receding water.

chapters.title: The Wreck of the Sable Fortune
chapters.summary: Vikram's POV. His ship grounds on the reef he came to plunder; Coral lands on the beach and pulls him and his diver out anyway. Vikram hands her the stolen manifest pages unprompted. Beat: honor found in the wreckage of greed.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. In a humid port authority office, Coral gives a new sworn statement: the forgery, her false testimony, Dez's confession recorded before the collapse. Rafe's conviction is vacated pending review. Beat: truth delivered at last, hands shaking, voice steady.

chapters.title: Grounded
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Her license suspended, her plane impounded as evidence, Coral waits — and discovers stillness doesn't kill her. Rafe walks free and asks nothing of her except the truth she already gave. Beat: reckoning without annihilation.

chapters.title: The Next Chart
chapters.summary: Coral and Ilsa's shared close. Months later, Ilsa leads the official survey of the now-drowned site; Coral, license restored, flies the survey team in — landing twice in the same place, on purpose. Beat: memory honored, love chosen, wheels finally allowed to stop.
